subject.title: [Feature]: Enrich message_sending hook with resolved target context

question: What resolved outbound target facts may ordinary loaded plugins receive on `message_sending`, and should that contract be nested as `targetContext` or exposed through a different Plugin SDK shape?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but exposing target kind, channel/account identity, externality, and cross-context status defines a public Plugin SDK contract and a security disclosure boundary.

options.title: Approve narrow target context
options.body: Expose only stable, policy-useful facts such as target kind, channel id, and cross-context/external booleans from existing resolver and policy state.

options.title: Keep the hook raw
options.body: Leave `message_sending` unchanged until a broader plugin policy and trust model decides what target-resolution details plugins may observe.

options.title: Use an explicit resolver helper
options.body: Document a supported plugin-side resolver path while accepting lookup cost and possible divergence from the exact runtime-resolved destination.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow target context
recommendation.body: Expose only stable, policy-useful facts such as target kind, channel id, and cross-context/external booleans from existing resolver and policy state.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a public SDK and security-disclosure boundary decision, and history ties this owner to outbound/security seam direction.
